title: Building effective agents
claim: Start with simple composable workflows and add complexity only when measured outcomes justify it.
limitations: Mutable vendor post; now warns its original tooling landscape changed. Its guidance is not a comparative media-evaluation experiment.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
claim: Distinguish tasks, trials, graders, traces, outcomes, agent harness and evaluation harness; combine deterministic, model and human grading.
limitations: Vendor operational guidance; no universal success threshold or proof that its examples transfer to generated-media judgment.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
claim: Multi-agent breadth-first research can benefit from parallel context, but their system consumed substantially more tokens; bounded delegation and human checks remain necessary.
limitations: Reported gains and roughly 15x chat token usage are internal workload results, not fixed multipliers or proof of superiority for media evals.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
claim: Current v3 compares 260 configurations across six benchmarks and reports architecture-task dependence, saturation and coordination overhead.
limitations: Latest inspected revision 2026-04-08. Earlier search snippets contained obsolete numerical results. No media-specific effectiveness guarantee.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
claim: In seven NLP benchmarks, voting explains much of debate gains; their theoretical model does not give debate an automatic expected-correctness improvement.
limitations: v2 revised 2025-10-23, arXiv comments report NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight. Theoretical assumptions and NLP scope limit transfer.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Multi-Agent Debate for LLM Judges with Adaptive Stability Detection
claim: A contrasting study reports gains from a specific debate judge and adaptive stopping scheme.
limitations: Different assumptions and benchmarks from H05; does not justify a universal debate policy, convergence as truth, or unbounded loops.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
claim: Study finds correct minorities in divergent debates and uses a learned classifier to decide when to overturn a majority.
limitations: Three heterogeneous agents, six benchmarks; arXiv reports workshop acceptance. Learned flip safety needs task-specific labels and replication.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Quantifying and Mitigating Self-Preference Bias of LLM Judges
claim: Across studied LLMs, capability does not guarantee low self-preference; structured multidimensional judging reduced measured bias.
limitations: v4 revised 2026-06-02. Constructed equal-quality text pairs do not establish unbiased media judgments.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Agreement Overstates Evidence: Error Dependence in LLM Judge Consensus
claim: Judge votes contain correlated errors; item-level inference and trusted validation are needed; full text does not support a universally superior learned voting rule.
limitations: Full limitations inspected: controlled regimes, position bias chiefly studied, trusted-label assumptions and limited judge banks. Published effect sizes are not this lab's calibration.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Can We Trust LLM Judges: A Study of Capability-Dependent Biases and Multi-Judge Ensemble for Bias Calibration
claim: Proposes label-free weighted voting from disagreement patterns and reports promising performance in a simulated shifting-distribution experiment.
limitations: Simulation and agreement-based estimator do not replace independent media labels; dependence assumptions must be evaluated.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Debiasing as a Measurement Intervention: Calibrated Ties and Resolution Loss in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
claim: Anti-citation bias instructions can suppress spurious preferences while converting meaningful quality differences to ties; report resolution as well as bias.
limitations: ArXiv comments report EMNLP 2026 acceptance. Diagnostic partly templated text benchmark; mostly two annotators; TRACE audit adds cost and extraction error.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: The Anatomy of Harness Engineering: How to Evaluate, Iterate, and Guard AI Coding Agents
claim: Small behavioral checks complement end-to-end evals; repeated batches help diagnose stochastic behavior without rigidly prescribing every tool sequence.
limitations: Coding-agent guidance. Its dogfood-first timing conflicts with eval-first guidance; our mandated Phase 4 offline tests take precedence.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Prompt caching benchmark: high cache reuse does not always mean lower cost
claim: Their multi-turn experiment shows cache-read fraction is insufficient to infer total cost; output volume, prices and latency must also be measured.
limitations: Day obtained from publisher blog index; article shows October 2026. Twenty shopping dialogues, repeated five times; model and provider changed together; costs are estimates unreconciled to bills.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
claim: Demonstrates distillation of selected specialized harness behaviors into model weights under a fixed target harness.
limitations: Knowledge, tool and science tasks; training experiment does not remove application authorization, budgets, audit, or prove transfer to media.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
claim: Limit functionality, permissions and autonomy; enforce authorization downstream rather than trusting model output.
limitations: Security guidance, not a certification or complete defense. Page retains 2025 title as accessed.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
claim: Agent security requires controlled tool access, least authority, validation and monitoring beyond prompt-only instructions.
limitations: Continuously maintained guidance; no claim that adopting the checklist eliminates prompt injection.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Inspect AI documentation
claim: Existing evaluation framework exposes tasks, datasets, solvers, scorers, sandboxing, limits, logs and extension points.
limitations: Framework capability documentation; adoption alone validates neither our graders nor media rubric. No dependency installed during research.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
claim: Current official repository defines GenAI spans, metrics and events; the old website section explicitly says moved and no longer maintained.
limitations: Moving specification with Schema URL marked TODO in inspected README. Pin a revision and map internal events; no blanket stability or compliance claim.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked

title: Pydantic Strict Mode
claim: Strict validation reduces coercion; JSON validation still has type-specific exceptions.
limitations: Type correctness does not imply truth, authorization, referential integrity or valid time ranges; custom domain checks remain needed.
verification: primary source opened; bibliographic metadata and claim checked
